messages:
emily: deploy-bot halted canary for release redwood-api 2.3.1 — image digest in Helm values doesn't match registry. canary pods evicted. anyone picking this up?

deploy-bot: [AUTO] Canary halted for release=redwood-api env=canary reason=image.digest.mismatch registry=ghcr.io/redwood/redwood-api:2.3.1 expected=sha256:abcd... actual=sha256:ef01... action=halt

raj: on it. quick question — did the build pipeline re-promote a new image tag or did someone update values.yaml manually?

maria: CI promoted a rebuilt artifact at 09:04, might have the same tag but different digest (mutable tag). values.yaml still references the old digest.

tom: Ugh, mutable tags again. Options: 1) rollback the canary to previous release, 2) patch canary values to match new digest and re-run smoke, 3) pin image tag to immutable digest and block auto-promote.

emily: Given we're in EMEA change window in ~35m, I'd prefer minimal blast radius — patch the canary values only, run smoke tests, then staged rollout.

raj: I can apply an override on the release in canary namespace instead of changing chart:

```bash
helm upgrade redwood-api-canary ./charts/redwood-api \
  --namespace canary \
  --reuse-values \
  --set image.digest=sha256:ef01... \
  --set image.tag=2.3.1
```

raj: That keeps main values untouched and lets us test the actual image the registry serves. If smoke fails, helm rollback redwood-api-canary 1.

maria: I'll run the smoke suite once you patch. If latency or error rate spikes >20% or >1% respectively, we rollback immediately. I'll watch traces and logs.

tom: Add a short release note/annotation so downstream automation doesn't auto-sync the old digest back: `kubectl annotate deployment/redwood-api canary.hotpatch=true --overwrite`

emily: Also create a follow-up PR to update chart values.yaml and update the build pipeline to publish immutable tags (or surface a digest file). We should also add a CI guard to fail a release if tag mutability detected.

raj: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/charts/pull/482 — updates values and adds a note about tag immutability. I'll include rollout steps in the PR description.

deploy-bot: Canary override applied by raj. smoke-run queued.

maria: smoke-run passed basic health checks (startup, readiness, simple query) but one regression alert popped on a noncritical path — investigating.

tom: If it's noncritical and trace looks harmless, proceed with staged 10% -> 50% rollout. If not, rollback.

emily: decision: hotpatch canary only, run staged promotion after 10m stable. If any error rate >0.8% we rollback. Maria owns monitoring, Raj owns the override and rollback steps, Tom owns release annotation and PR.

maria: acknowledged, I'll post updates in this thread.

raj: if we need to rollback quickly: `helm rollback redwood-api-canary 1 && kubectl annotate deployment/redwood-api canary.hotpatch=removed`

emily: thanks — keeping this thread as the single source. we'll merge the PR after post-mortem. :thumbsup:
